messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: prefix-cache hit_rate drop > 30% for model-serving-prod in us-west-2 over the last 2m. paging @sre-lisa
sre-lisa: acked. I’m looking. tagging logs and metric links — https://obs.example.com/rum?query=prefix_cache.hitrate%3C0.7&from=now-5m
paul-eng: seen the page, jumping in. any customer SLO hits reported?
emma-support: flagging 3 current customers with elevated latencies: acme-corp, swiftchat, edu.ai. Support ticket IDs #3421 #3422 #3423. No error rate spike yet, mostly latency and a few timeouts.
carol-infra: seeing correlated increase in eviction_count on the kv nodes (nodepool-prefix-1..4). Evictions spiked ~18:32 UTC. Possible bulk invalidation job? checking control plane audit.
ben-ml: model-serving traces show higher model cold-starts because kv prefix miss. Requests that would normally hit cache are going to backend. could be cache invalidation or namespace mixup.
sre-lisa: quick mitigation idea: throttle invalidation job + roll back last deploy of prefix-invalidator. Does anyone know if there was a config change pushed ~18:30?
carol-infra: there was a config push: infra-deploy pipeline 2026-03-15T18:27 - changed ttl default for prefix cache from 120 -> 0 (was intended for canary). pipeline logs: https://ci.example.com/builds/4721
paul-eng: oh. that explains it. TTL->0 effectively disables prefix reuse; hit rate collapse matches. can we revert TTL to 120 immediately?
devex-zoe: reversion runbook: `kubectl set env deployment/prefix-service PREFIX_TTL=120 -n infra-prod && kubectl rollout restart deployment/prefix-service -n infra-prod`
sre-lisa: executing now. also enabling a temporary local caching layer on edge to absorb requests. will post rollout status.
oncall-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout rollback for deployment/prefix-service by sre-lisa at 18:39:12 UTC
sre-lisa: rollback command completed, pods restarting. watching metrics.
paul-eng: adding a short-term mitigation: enable request-level KV memoization for 60s (`--kv-prefix-cache=60`) to reduce backend load while rollout completes.
ben-ml: note: even with TTL revert, we need to confirm KV cache reuse behavior — history shows some shards don't pick up the new TTL until full restart; validate per-pod env.
carol-infra: checking pods: pod/prefix-service-5a2 (nodepool-2) still has PREFIX_TTL=0. I’m forcing a restart for that pod.
emma-support: customer impact update: latencies for acme-corp dropped from ~1.8s to ~400ms after initial rollout started. Sending messages to affected customers with ETA 10m for full remediation. :thumbsup:
sre-lisa: metrics: prefix hit_rate back to 0.82 across region in 3m after restarts. eviction_count trending down. marking mitigation: TTL reverted + pod restarts.
oncall-bot: incident-bot: Mitigation applied: env rollback + pod restarts + short-term kv memoization. Impact: degraded latency for subset of traffic. Incident severity: Sev2 -> moving to followup.
paul-eng: before we close, collect artifacts for RCA: - pipeline change that set TTL to 0 (link) - who approved canary change? - per-pod env propagation logs - hit-rate timeline from obs - requests that experienced backend fallback (traces)
ben-ml: hypothesis tracking: H1: accidental canary config pushed to prod (LIKELY). H2: TTL change rolled but some pods didn't restart causing staggered hit-rate recovery (POSSIBLE). H3: unrelated KV eviction storm triggered by memory pressure (UNLIKELY given patch timing).
devex-zoe: I’ll open a timeline doc and add owners. Doc: https://docs.example.com/rca/prefix-ttl-surge-1845123456
sre-lisa: timeline notes (adding here for thread): 18:27 config pipeline sets PREFIX_TTL=0 -> 18:31 eviction spike observed -> 18:32 alert triggered -> 18:34 oncall page -> 18:39 rollback started -> 18:42 pods restarted -> 18:45 hit_rate recovered.
carol-infra: saved relevant logs: `kubectl logs deployment/prefix-service --since=20m > /tmp/prefix-logs-1845.log` — uploaded to artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/incidents/1845123456/prefix-logs.tar.gz
ben-ml: small sample trace when miss occurred:
```
trace_id: 0x9f1a
route: /v1/generate
cache.lookup(prefix=0x7f2) -> MISS
kv.fetch shard=3 -> 504ms
model.call -> +120ms
response total -> 1.9s
```
paul-eng: action items (owner): - infra: pipeline gating and canary scoping (carol-infra) - eng: add pre-deploy check to prevent TTL=0 in prod (paul-eng) - ops: add automated env-propagation check post-deploy (sre-lisa)
emma-support: I'll consolidate customer comms and attach to doc.
devex-zoe: note for postmortem: include replay of the change and show canary isolation failure. Also include the mitigation steps and time-to-recover graph.
sre-lisa: assigning postmortem lead to paul-eng. please include the following in RCA: root cause, timeline, why TTL=0 was allowed, why rollout didn't restart all pods, why alerts didn't block the pipeline push, and customer impact timeline.
paul-eng: will do. expected draft by EOD tomorrow. tagging reviewers: @carol-infra @ben-ml @emma-support
oncall-bot: incident-bot: Incident moved to postmortem. If regressions occur, reopen thread or page oncall.
sre-lisa: closing on-call for this incident. leaving followups in doc. Thanks all for the quick response. :heart:
